subject: First flood call: storm drain backup

dialog.body: City of Newport, Kevin speaking.
Hi, this is Eleanor Pucci, at the end of Thames Street in the Fifth Ward. The storm drain on my corner backed up in yesterday's storm and I have water in my basement.
I'm sorry to hear that. Is anyone hurt, or any water near electrical?
No, nobody's hurt. It's just a mess. Boxes, the washer, all of it.
Okay. I'm opening a request for Public Works to look at the drain. Someone will call you back this week to set up a time.
This week. All right.
Anything else I can help with today?
No. Thank you, Kevin.

subject: Storm drain backup, basement flooded, water and sewer payment

dialog.body: City of Newport, this is Dana. How can I help you this morning?

Hi. My name is Eleanor Pucci, I'm down at the end of Thames Street in the Fifth Ward. The storm drain on my corner backed up again after last week's nor'easter and my basement flooded. That's the second time this winter.
I'm sorry, Mrs. Pucci. Second time this winter, you said?
Second time. I took the morning off to call because nobody called me back the first time. I'm done being patient about this.
Understood. Let me pull up your address. While I have you, I see an overdue water and sewer balance of ninety dollars on the account.
I know. I got the letter about the lien. I want to clear it today. Can I pay by card?
Yes, I can take that now. Go ahead with the card number when you're ready.
It's 4111 1111 1111 1111, expiration twelve twenty-eight.
Thank you. That ninety dollars has posted and your account is clear. Now, on the drain. I'm putting in a work order for Public Works. I can get a crew out to your corner Thursday.
Thursday. And is anyone going to call me this time?
Yes. I'm also asking a supervisor to call you back before then, so you hear it from someone who can do something about it.
So Thursday, and someone calls me?
Thursday for the crew, and a supervisor call before that. You have my word.
All right. Thank you, Dana.

subject: Crew radio call: Thames Street drain

dialog.body: Dispatch, it's Marcus. We're at the Thames Street corner on the Pucci work order.
Go ahead, Marcus.
Grate's clear. We pulled a lot of leaves and sand out and the water's moving for now.
But I put the camera down the line. The pipe under the street is collapsed about twenty feet in. That's not a cleaning job. That's a rebuild.
Okay. So do I close the work order?
Close the cleaning. Somebody needs to open something for the line. I told her it's a temporary fix. Next big storm, it backs up again.
I'll mark it cleared and pass the rest to the supervisor.
Thanks, Paula.

subject: Third call: drain nearly backed up again

dialog.body: City of Newport, this is Dana.
Dana, it's Eleanor Pucci again, on Thames Street. It rained all night. The water came right up to the top of the drain on my corner. It held this time, but barely.
I'm glad it held. Let me look you up.
The crew that came in February told me the pipe under the street is broken. Nobody has called me about fixing it. And the supervisor never called me either.
I see the work order from February. It shows the drain was cleared and the order is closed. Our records show that was fixed.
The man who fixed it told me it wasn't fixed. That's the whole point.
I'm sorry. I'll put a note in and ask Public Works to call you.
That's what I was told last time. Thank you, Dana.
